text:
maria: Heads-up — infra wants to finalise trace retention rules today. We need a concrete policy for hot vs cold traces across envs (prod/dogfood/staging/dev). Any strong opinions?

mike: +1. Quick context: storage cost is spiking because hot storage keeps 30d for prod and we index everything. We should consider moving older spans to a cheaper blob store and keep only minimal index for queries.

jenna: Agree. We already export OTLP to collector -> tempo-ish backend. Two knobs: TTL for full-indexed hot tier and TTL for cheap cold tier (read-only). Also whether to keep a short-term index (trace id -> blob pointer).

arjun: Proposal: prod: 14d hot (full traces + indexes), 90d cold (blobs, limited indices), 1y archive (optional, costed). dogfood: 7d hot, 30d cold. staging/dev: 3d hot, 14d cold or just keep blobs for 30d.

maria: That’s a big change from current 30d hot for prod. What’s the impact on debugging latency for recent regressions?

mike: Practically, most debug sessions look at <7d. Beyond 14d we rarely need full flamegraphs quickly. Cold reads will be slower (seconds), but still usable.

jenna: We should also consider a sliding window for sampling: reduce sampling rate for traces older than X days (e.g., keep 100% for 0-3d, 50% for 3-14d, 10% for 14-90d). That keeps hot index density down.

oliver: Ops concern: automatic tiering requires idempotent eviction. Make sure the OTEL collector and exporter metadata include the storage pointer. Also we need deterministic compaction job.

arjun: Example retention config (draft):
```
retention:
  prod:
    hot_days: 14
    cold_days: 90
    archive_days: 365
    sampling:
      0-3: 1.0
      3-14: 0.5
      14-90: 0.1
  staging:
    hot_days: 3
    cold_days: 30
    sampling:
      0-3: 1.0
      3-30: 0.2
```

arjun: The collector can attach a "storage-tier" attribute to spans for easier routing during ingest.

jenna: Ops-bot: note — any retention change needs to be announced and include a fallback in case a canary alerts.

ops-bot: Reminder: update the telemetry-runbook and notify on-call two weeks before enforcement.

sara: Two questions: 1) How do we handle customer PII in old spans? 2) Where do we store cold blobs (S3 vs Glacier class)?

mike: PII: we need to ensure scrubbing happens before coldification. Cold blobs should be stored in S3 IA or Glacier as a cost trade-off; keep a cheap index in hot store.

oliver: Also add a per-customer override for compliance customers (e.g., longer hot retention behind dedicated billing).

maria: Sounds good. Action items: (1) arjun to draft exact config + migration plan, (2) jenna to prototype sampler + collector attr, (3) oliver to define compaction/eviction job, (4) mike to cost model S3 IA vs Glacier and impact on query latency.

mike: I’ll run numbers by EOD tomorrow. Suggest we target gradual rollout to prod in 4 weeks with a 2-week observability canary.

jenna: For rollout UX — console should show per-environment retention + a timeline visualization, and a toggle for immediate pinning of a trace to hot tier (manual preserve).

arjun: One more: we should export span-level lineage metadata so cold reads can rehydrate quickly into the temporary query cache.

maria: Thanks everyone — ping me if you need approvals. I’ll schedule a short sync Friday to sign off on the final policy.
